import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Fill missing values in 'Sleep Disorder' with 'None' for clarity
df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None', inplace=True)

# Ensure categorical columns have a logical order for plotting
df['BMI Category'] = pd.Categorical(
    df['BMI Category'],
    categories=['Normal', 'Overweight', 'Obese'],
    ordered=True
)
df['Sleep Disorder'] = pd.Categorical(
    df['Sleep Disorder'],
    categories=['None', 'Insomnia', 'Sleep Apnea'],
    ordered=True
)

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
sns.set_context("talk", font_scale=0.8)

# Create a color palette
palette = {'None': '#3a5a40', 'Insomnia': '#e07a5f', 'Sleep Apnea': '#3d405b'}

# Create a faceted violin plot to show distribution and relationships
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='Stress Level',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',
    col='BMI Category',
    kind='violin',
    palette=palette,
    height=6,
    aspect=1.1,
    inner='quartile', # Show quartiles inside the violins
    split=False, # Draw separate violins for each hue level
    legend_out=True
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set a comprehensive title for the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle(
    'Sleep Quality is Inversely Related to Stress, Exacerbated by Sleep Disorders and BMI',
    y=1.04,
    fontsize=20,
    weight='bold'
)

# Set axis labels
g.set_axis_labels("Stress Level (1-10)", "Quality of Sleep (1-10)", fontsize=14)

# Set titles for each subplot
g.set_titles("BMI Category: {col_name}", size=16)

# Improve legend
g.legend.set_title("Sleep Disorder Status")
plt.setp(g.legend.get_texts(), fontsize='12')
plt.setp(g.legend.get_title(), fontsize='14')

# Add annotations to highlight a key insight
# This part is illustrative; specific coordinates might need adjustment
# based on the exact data distribution.
ax1 = g.axes[0, 1] # Target the 'Overweight' subplot
ax1.text(
    x=5.5, y=3.5,
    s='Higher stress levels correlate\nwith poorer sleep quality,\n especially for those with\n existing sleep disorders.',
    horizontalalignment='center',
    size=11,
    color='#58508d',
    bbox=dict(facecolor='white', alpha=0.6, boxstyle="round,pad=0.5")
)

# Adjust layout to prevent title overlap
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Close the plot to prevent it from displaying in some environments
plt.close()
